title: m-4: port010-site-allow
description:
## Goal
#786 S8 and the other shapes beyond S3/S6: PORT-010 must be allowable at a single site. An item carrying #[sc_lint(allow(PORT-010), reason = "...")] is not reported by PORT-010 (ADR-022 decision 4). This is the exception path for deliberate POSIX-only public helpers such as current_uid and is_owned_by_uid.
## Deliverables
1. Directive grammar (design): add Directive::SiteAllow { rules, reason }, separate from Allow. Rule ids are unquoted tokens (PORT-010); reason = "..." is required and non-empty. boundary.* directives parse exactly as before (frozen corpus test unchanged); boundary ignores SiteAllow and portability ignores boundary.* directives.
2. Portability honours it: PORT-010 does not report an item carrying #[sc_lint(...)] or #[sc_lint_attributes::sc_lint(...)] with allow(PORT-010). The allowance covers only that item; an allow on an impl block does not cascade to its methods, and nothing covers a module's contents, a file or a sibling.
3. Errors: malformed site allows and unknown PORT rule ids are typed errors with file and line; ids owned by other analyzers are ignored by portability.
4. Report: FindingsReport gains an optional allowed array (omitted when empty, no schema_version change) with item, source_path, line, rule_id and reason for each allowance that suppressed a finding.
5. Tests: port010_site_allow (annotated pub #[cfg(unix)] fn current_uid not reported, unannotated sibling reported, one allowed entry), site_allow_grammar_corpus (every accepted and rejected form in the design table), site_allow_unknown_rule, site_allow_no_cascade. Fold analyzer isolation and omission-when-empty assertions into the frozen directive corpus and existing json_contract tests. Include stacked cfg/doc/inline attributes, an inherent impl method and a public function in port010_site_allow.
6. Keep sc-lint-attributes a no-op for behavior and public API; it builds on stable Linux, macOS and Windows through the existing CI matrix. Document adoption in docs-bundle/packages/sc-lint-portability.md: add the sc-lint-attributes dependency and list it in each consumer crate's boundary allowed_dependencies so SCB-DEPENDENCY stays clean. Every allowance reason names the item's actual cause.
## Does Not Close
No repository-wide switch, path exclusion or blanket suppression of PORT-010. Extending allow to other analyzers is later ADR-022 work.
## Active Trace
ANC-010, ANC-009. ADR-022 decision 4; ADR-010 amendment 2026-10-30 (per-site allowance).
design:
Baseline: sc-lint-directives/src/lib.rs has Directive { Allow(Vec<String>), InternalOnly, ForbidExternalImpls } and parses only <scope>.<action> (parse_scope accepts only boundary); sc-lint-attributes provides the no-op #[sc_lint]; sc-lint-boundary/src/graph/mod.rs:25-52 matches exhaustively over Directive; portability reads no directives; FindingsReport<R> (sc-lint-schema/src/lib.rs:237) has tool, version, schema_version, status, scanned_crates, findings and is rendered by sc-lint-analyzer-support/src/render.rs.
Grammar (token level, the same parser in the attribute macro and both analyzers):
```
args      := element ("," element)* ","?
element   := scoped | site_allow | reason
scoped    := "boundary" "." action          // unchanged
site_allow:= "allow" "(" rule_id ("," rule_id)* ","? ")"
rule_id   := IDENT "-" INT                  // PORT - 010 tokens, normalized to "PORT-010"
reason    := "reason" "=" STRING            // non-empty after trim
```
| Input | Result |
| allow(PORT-010), reason = "x" | SiteAllow { rules: [PORT-010], reason: "x" } |
| reason = "x", allow(PORT-010) | same (order free) |
| allow(PORT-010, PORT-011), reason = "x" | two rules, one reason |
| allow(PORT-010) | error: missing reason |
| allow(PORT-010), reason = "  " | error: empty reason |
| allow("PORT-010"), reason = "x" | error: rule id must be unquoted |
| allow(PORT-010, PORT-010), reason = "x" | error: duplicate rule id |
| reason = "x" | error: reason without allow |
| two allow(...) elements | error: one allow per attribute |
| boundary.allow("B"), allow(PORT-010), reason = "x" | both directives |
Unquoted ids follow ADR-022 decision 4 syntax; boundary ids stay quoted strings because they name boundary records, not rules.
```rust
pub enum Directive { Allow(Vec<String>), InternalOnly, ForbidExternalImpls, SiteAllow { rules: Vec<String>, reason: String } }
pub enum DirectiveError { /* existing */ MissingReason, EmptyReason, QuotedRuleId, DuplicateRuleId, ReasonWithoutAllow, MultipleAllow }
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct AllowedEntry { pub item: String, pub source_path: String, pub line: usize, pub rule_id: String, pub reason: String }
// FindingsReport: #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub allowed: Vec<AllowedEntry>
```
Error surface: the #[sc_lint] macro emits compile_error! with the DirectiveError text; portability returns PortabilityError::InvalidSiteAllow { path, line, error } and PortabilityError::UnknownRule { path, line, rule }, which take the existing analyzer configuration-error exit path. The rule catalog is portability's RuleId (lib.rs:67, CatalogRuleId list at 39). A stale allowance (suppresses nothing) is not listed and not an error. parity.rs consults a single call site_allow::allowance_for(item_attrs, RuleId::Port010) before emitting; the allowed entry travels with the findings through portability.rs and findings.rs to the report. sc-lint-portability gains a dependency on sc-lint-directives: update boundaries/sc-lint-directives/directive-model.toml allowed_dependents and boundaries/sc-lint-portability/portability-analyzer.toml allowed_dependencies, Cargo.toml and graph/mod.rs. Update docs/sc-lint-directives/requirements.md with the grammar.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
- issue:#786 S8: an item annotated #[sc_lint(allow(PORT-010), reason = "...")] produces no PORT-010 finding and appears in allowed with its reason; an unannotated sibling in the same file is still reported (port010_site_allow).
- Every row of the grammar table behaves as specified (site_allow_grammar_corpus); unknown PORT ids are typed errors; an impl-block allow does not cover its methods; boundary.* parsing and boundary results are unchanged; the frozen directive corpus and existing json_contract tests cover analyzer isolation and omission of an empty allowed array.
- Boundary inventories admit the new portability -> directives edge and the boundary check passes; docs/sc-lint-directives/requirements.md documents the grammar.
- atm-core sign-off 01M69P0C2R3S1BH78TYKHM9RPW: port010_site_allow covers stacked cfg/doc/inline attributes, an inherent impl method and a pub fn. sc-lint-attributes remains a no-op for behavior/public API and builds in the existing stable Linux/macOS/Windows CI matrix. Adoption docs explain dependency/boundary registration and item-specific reasons.
## Validation
- cargo test -p sc-lint-directives -p sc-lint-attributes -p sc-lint-boundary -p sc-lint-schema -p sc-lint-analyzer-support -p sc-lint-portability -p sc-lint --no-fail-fast
- just lint
- just test
Record the new tests failing on the develop baseline first.
